roadmap.goal: Bug #5567: the backend anchors "today" at UTC. The codebase models "store instants in UTC" with a first-class, enforced, tested abstraction (two `UtcDateTimeConverter` classes plus seven `Kind == Utc` tests) and models "compute a calendar day" with nothing at all — so 49 production sites each re-derived the anchor from the ambient clock, 12 of them via server-local `DateTime.Today` and 37 via `DateTime.UtcNow.Date`. Introduce `ILighthouseClock` as the single named seam for the instance's calendar day, configured by `Lighthouse:TimeZone`, converge `DeliveryMetricSnapshot` on a `DateOnly` day key so the last instant-bucketed snapshot table matches its three siblings, migrate all 49 anchor sites plus the 8 Finding-F instant-to-day reduction sites onto the clock, and make the seam enforceable with a source guard so no 50th site can appear. Deliberately NOT a general date refactor: ~30 genuine instant sites (audit stamps, sync bookkeeping, blocked-transition intervals, artifact naming, elapsed-duration measurement) stay UTC and step 03-01 proves they were not moved.
roadmap.overview: Four phases, 13 steps, one commit per step, each independently green. Phase 01 builds the seam without touching a single call site: 01-01 pins the backend test timezone via `.runsettings` and lands T0 — a test that fails on today's HEAD with ZERO production changes, because `ForecastController.cs:60` reads `DateTime.Today` while `:85/:86/:94/:133` read `DateTime.UtcNow.Date` in the same request; 01-02 introduces `ILighthouseClock` + `Lighthouse:TimeZone` + `FakeLighthouseClock`, shipping NO default value so containers keep UTC and standalone picks up the host zone; 01-03 lands the source guard in warn-list mode with all 49 known sites baselined, so the migration cannot race a 50th. Phase 02 migrates by cluster, shrinking the baseline each time, in the RCA §6 order with one insertion: entities first (highest blast radius, smallest change set), then the `DeliveryMetricSnapshot` day-key convergence and its expand-only migration (inserted so the snapshot handlers migrate ONTO an already-correct day key rather than onto one that changes under them), then the snapshot handlers, then metrics/forecast controllers, then Finding F, then demo data, then validation/licensing/delivery. Phase 03 flips the guard to hard-fail and sweeps the remaining tautological tests. Phase 04 documents the setting, the API date semantics and the release-note headline — which, because the shipped default is ABSENT, is that non-UTC teams must OPT IN via `Lighthouse__TimeZone`. RED comes first in every phase-02 step: the test asserting the instance-zone day is written against `FakeLighthouseClock` BEFORE the call sites move, and the tests in each cluster are migrated in the SAME commit as their production code — otherwise they re-tautologise against the new expression (RCA §1D, §6.6).

amendment_findings.r2_duplicate_row_is_not_reachable_at_hea: MATERIAL, because it is the sole stated rationale for the Q3 schema change. The RCA §7-R2 claim is that `DeliveryMetricSnapshotRepository.cs:12-18` 'buckets a full instant into a day by range scan, so shifting the zone can make an existing row fall outside [day, nextDay) and produce a SECOND row for the same visual day rather than an upsert.' Verified at HEAD, the duplicate cannot occur: (a) `GetOrCreateForDay` NORMALISES on write — line 12 computes `var day = recordedAt.Date;` and line 25 constructs `new DeliveryMetricSnapshot { RecordedAt = day }`, so every persisted `RecordedAt` is midnight, never a mid-day instant, even though `DeliveryMetricSnapshotRecordingHandler.cs:30` passes a full `DateTime.UtcNow`; (b) `GetOrCreateForDay` is the ONLY production writer — a repo-wide search for `RecordedAt =` on this type finds no other production assignment, only test seeding; (c) `Data/LighthouseAppContext.cs:400-401` already declares `HasIndex(s => new { s.DeliveryId, s.RecordedAt }).IsUnique()`, so the database itself forbids two rows for the same delivery and the same midnight. The range scan over midnight-valued data is therefore exactly equivalent to equality on a day key. What a zone shift CAN actually produce is a one-day SKIP or SHIFT in the 22:00-24:00 UTC window where the instance day is already tomorrow — the same artifact the RCA explicitly accepts for the three `DateOnly`-keyed families, and a one-day kink in the trend chart either way. THE SCHEMA CHANGE IS STILL WORTH DOING and is retained as instructed, on the honest rationale rather than the stated one: it makes the day key structurally a day (`DateOnly` is untouched by the global `Properties<DateTime>()` converter convention, so R1 cannot reach it at all), it removes the last instant-to-day reduction living inside a repository, and it converges all four snapshot tables on one shape — `BlockedCountSnapshot.cs:13` and `PercentilesOverTimeSnapshot.cs:22` already declare `public DateOnly RecordedAt`. Step 02-02's criteria are written against that rationale. They do NOT claim to fix a duplicate row, because a test asserting 'no duplicate is created' would pass on unmodified HEAD and prove nothing.
amendment_findings.unique_index_makes_the_backfill_a_deploy: The expand-only migration must add a unique index on the new (DeliveryId, day) pair to preserve the guarantee `(DeliveryId, RecordedAt)` gives today. If ANY existing row carries a non-midnight `RecordedAt` — impossible via the current writer, but not impossible via an older version, a restored backup, or manual data — two rows can backfill to the same `DateOnly` and the unique-index creation FAILS mid-migration, which on this project means the application does not start. This is encoded as an explicit acceptance criterion in 02-02 (prove the migration against a database seeded with a colliding non-midnight row and decide the collision policy deliberately) rather than left to be discovered on a customer's upgrade.
amendment_findings.expand_only_is_machine_enforced_here: `Lighthouse.Backend.Tests/Architecture/ExpandOnlyMigrationGuard.cs` and its companion `ExpandOnlyMigrationGuardTest.cs` already exist and enforce the additive-only rule automatically. The Q3 migration will be checked by it with no new tooling, and 02-02 asserts it stays green rather than restating the rule by hand. Precedent migration tests for the sibling snapshot tables exist at `Lighthouse.Backend.Tests/Integration/Containers/BlockedCountSnapshotMigrationTests.cs`, `PercentilesOverTimeSnapshotMigrationTests.cs` and `ProcessBehaviorSnapshotMigrationTests.cs` — 02-02's migration test follows their shape.

hard_constraints: R1 / DESIGN §4.1 constraint 1 — `ILighthouseClock` MUST NEVER return a `DateTime` whose `Kind` is `Local`. The global EF converter (`Data/Converters/UtcDateTimeConverter.cs`, applied as a convention at `Data/LighthouseAppContext.cs:91-92`) applies `ToUniversalTime()` to every non-`Unspecified` `DateTime` property AND to query parameters. A Local-kind local-midnight written to a snapshot timestamp is shifted back by the offset on write, lands on the previous UTC day, and re-introduces this exact bug through the persistence layer — with reads staying self-consistent while the stored data silently goes wrong for every other consumer. `Today` is `DateOnly`; the only `DateTime` the clock hands out is `TodayAsUtcMidnight`, `Kind = Utc`. This is the most likely way the fix ships broken.

DESIGN §4.1 constraint 2 — pure functions and EF-materialised entities take `DateOnly today` AS A PARAMETER; they never receive an injected clock. `Team.GetThroughputSettings()`, `Feature.GetLikelhoodForDate()`, `Delivery.CalculateMetrics()` and `WorkItemBase.WorkItemAge` become parameterised, matching the existing `blackoutPeriods` parameter-passing style at `Models/Delivery.cs:99`.

Branch B is NOT PROVABLE BY ANY RUNTIME TEST: `DateTime.Today` and `DateTime.UtcNow.Date` diverge only in real wall-clock time, and time cannot be injected into code that reads the clock statically (that is root cause D restated). Verified empirically by un-ignoring T0 on HEAD: the two endpoints AGREED (both returned the real current date) and only the expected-anchor-day assertions failed, because the injected `FakeTimeProvider` instant never reaches production. criteria: THE OPT-IN IS THE HEADLINE, NOT A FOOTNOTE. steps.implementation_notes: RCA §9, amended for Q1 and Q3. Root cause E in one sentence: `b956a8857` made the client half of the date contract consistently local while the backend stayed UTC, and NOTHING anywhere said which reading was correct — so the fix that made the frontend right made the asymmetry sharper rather than milder. Documentation here is not a formality; it is the artefact that stops the next author re-deriving the wrong answer. THE Q1 DECISION CHANGES THIS STEP'S CENTRE OF GRAVITY: with the key shipped absent, the release is deliberately inert for the users who reported the bug until they act, so documentation is not describing the fix — it IS the delivery mechanism for it. A release note that buries the opt-in in a configuration section ships a fix nobody turns on. Per the project's per-feature discipline, docs land WITH the feature and not deferred to `/release`; the standing rule is also that docs updates wait for the user's confirmation in their own environment, so treat this step as ready-to-write rather than auto-push. The ci-learnings entry follows the file's own template (Symptom / Root cause / Fix / Rule going forward) and — per the note at `docs/ci-learnings.md:45-51` — the NON-GREPPABLE rules should be folded up into the Preflight checklist, not merely appended as a dated entry, because the append-only log demonstrably does not get re-applied. There is no obvious greppable ledger-check pattern to add: `DateTime.UtcNow.Date` in production is now covered by the 03-01 source guard, and the `DateOnly` day-key rule is covered by its type-level assertion — both stronger mechanisms than a staged-diff grep.
